emails.subject: URGENT: Your account will be LOCKED in 1 hour
emails.body: We detected unusual activity. Verify your password now or lose access to your account forever.
emails.explanation: Real banks never ask for your password by email, and panic deadlines are a classic pressure trick.

emails.subject: Congratulations!!! You won a free tablet
emails.body: You were randomly selected! Just pay $4.99 shipping to claim your prize today.
emails.explanation: You can't win a contest you never entered — 'small fee' prizes are just a way to steal card details.

emails.subject: Mailbox full - action required
emails.body: Your mailbox is 99% full. Log in below within 24 hours or your emails will be deleted.
emails.explanation: Your real IT team writes from your organization's domain, not a free email account.

emails.subject: Package on hold: unpaid customs fee
emails.body: Your parcel can't be delivered. Pay the $1.95 customs fee to reschedule.
emails.explanation: Look closely: 'she11ship' uses the number 1 twice instead of the letter L.

emails.subject: Quick favor - keep this confidential
emails.body: I'm in a meeting. Buy 5 gift cards for a client and send me the codes. I'll pay you back.
emails.explanation: No real boss asks for gift card codes by email — this is a famous 'CEO fraud' scam.

emails.subject: Payment declined - update your billing info
emails.body: We couldn't process your last payment. Update your card to keep watching.
clues: Link text doesn't match real URL
emails.explanation: The link SAYS tidewatch.com but really goes to a different site — always check where a link goes.

emails.subject: 2027 salary adjustment - review attached
emails.body: Please review your updated salary document. Enable editing to view.
emails.explanation: '.docm' files can run hidden code — 'enable editing to view' is how malware gets in.

emails.subject: Maria shared 'Invoice_Q4.pdf' with you
emails.body: You have a new shared document. Sign in with your email password to open it.
emails.explanation: File-sharing scams fake a document so you'll type your email password into their page.

emails.subject: You are eligible for a $742.18 refund
emails.body: Submit your bank details within 48 hours to receive your refund.
emails.explanation: Government agencies don't email you asking for bank details — and their sites end in .gov.

emails.subject: New sign-in from a new device
emails.body: We noticed a new sign-in. If this wasn't you, review your activity.
clues: Real domain is at the END: secure-login.net
emails.explanation: Read domains from the right: this is really 'secure-login.net' wearing the bank's name as a disguise.

emails.subject: Re: updated logo files
emails.body: Hey! Here are the final logo files from today's meeting, let me know what you think.
emails.explanation: '.pdf.exe' is a program pretending to be a PDF — opening it would run malware.

emails.subject: Your verification code
emails.body: Someone is trying to recover your account. Reply with the 6-digit code we just texted you to stop them.
clues: Asks you to share a 2FA code
emails.explanation: Never share a verification code — anyone asking for it is the person trying to break in.

emails.subject: Dinner Sunday?
emails.body: Are you free Sunday at 6? I'm making plov. Bring a friend if you want!
clues: No links, no requests for money or info
emails.explanation: A normal message from someone you know, asking nothing risky — totally safe.

emails.subject: Reminder: book due Friday
emails.body: Your book 'Intro to Networks' is due Friday. You can renew it from your library account.
emails.explanation: Real sender, matching link, and no urgency or requests — a normal reminder.

emails.subject: Notes from today
emails.body: Uploaded my notes to our shared folder. See you Thursday!
emails.explanation: A classmate sharing notes, no links or demands — safe.

emails.subject: New this week: 5 shows we think you'll love
emails.body: Here's what's new this week. Happy watching!
emails.explanation: A regular newsletter: real domain, honest link, and it doesn't ask you for anything.

emails.subject: Holiday hours
emails.body: We'll close at 4pm on Thursday for the holiday. Normal hours resume Friday.
emails.explanation: Pure information with nothing to click or give — safe.

emails.subject: Your November statement is ready
emails.body: Your statement is ready. Sign in through our app or by typing bluefinbank.com into your browser.
clues: Tells you to go to the site yourself
emails.explanation: Good sign: the bank tells you to open the site yourself instead of clicking a login link.

emails.subject: Your package was delivered
emails.body: Your package was delivered at 2:14 PM and left at the front door.
emails.explanation: Compare with the scam version: correct 'shellship' spelling and nothing to pay.

emails.subject: Homework 4 posted
emails.body: Homework 4 is posted on the course site. Due next Tuesday before class.
emails.explanation: Expected attachment, plain .pdf, from your real professor's address — safe.

emails.subject: You're using 80% of your storage
emails.body: You're close to your storage limit. You can manage files anytime in the Driftbox app.
emails.explanation: A calm heads-up from the real domain with no threat and no login link.

emails.subject: New sign-in to your account
emails.body: New sign-in on a new phone. If this was you, no action needed. If not, open the Bluefin app to secure your account.
clues: Sends you to the app, not a link
emails.explanation: Real alerts often look scary too — but this one uses the real domain and no login link.

emails.subject: Scheduled maintenance Saturday 2–4 AM
emails.body: Email may be briefly unavailable during maintenance. No action is needed from you.
emails.explanation: Real IT notices usually say 'no action needed' — they inform, they don't demand.

emails.subject: Re: updated logo files
emails.body: Final logo files from today's meeting are in the shared team folder.
emails.explanation: Compare with the trap: right domain, a plain .pdf, and it matches a real meeting.
